question: A 35-year-old man presents to the emergency department with acute severe right loin-to-groin colicky pain and microscopic haematuria. He is afebrile. Which investigation is the gold standard for confirming the diagnosis and planning management?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IVU has largely been replaced by CT KUB; it uses contrast and takes longer, making it less suitable in the acute setting.

answers.text: Non-contrast CT of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder (NCCT KUB)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NCCT KUB is the gold standard for ureteric colic — it identifies stone size, site, and degree of obstruction rapidly, without contrast, with near 100% sensitivity and specificity.
Ultrasound can detect hydronephrosis but frequently misses small ureteric stones, especially mid-ureteric; NCCT is far more accurate for acute colic.
MRI is poor at detecting calcium stones and takes too long in the acute setting; NCCT is the investigation of choice.

overallFeedback.feedback: NCCT KUB is the gold standard for suspected ureteric colic. Ultrasound misses many stones; IVU is outdated; MRI is inappropriate for calcium stones.
Correct. NCCT KUB — no contrast, fast, near-perfect accuracy for ureteric stones.
